notes: CBRM's use tables are the reason this file exists. Their rows are named after the use rather than numbered, so the matrix machinery skipped them and each row flattened to text - 'Dwelling, Two Unit P P P P P P'. The table has no entry for R6, so those six marks shift one zone left and the row then says two-unit dwellings are permitted in R6, where the bylaw grants nothing, and not in R7, where it does.

The two-unit-dwelling question therefore asserts R7 is present and R6 is absent. It fails in both directions: if the row is flattened again, or if a blank cell is ever read as a prohibition rather than as an absence of entry.

The commercial table has three zone columns against a five-column minimum, which made its real header unrecognisable and let a row of 'P's stand in as the column names. That reached the database once; the zone-symbol question is what would have caught it.

questions.question: Which zones allow a two unit dwelling?
questions.why: The row with a blank cell. R7 must be named; naming R6 instead is the shift this file exists to catch.

questions.question: What uses are permitted in the mixed-use corridor commercial zone?
questions.why: The commercial table's real zone codes. A row of P's once stood in as its headings, and every mark was reported against a zone called P.

questions.question: How big can a secondary suite be?
questions.why: A numbered heading with a trailing period (4.19.), which no other municipality writes and which matched nothing until CBRM got its own scheme.

questions.question: What counts as a one unit dwelling?
questions.why: Definitions are unnumbered here and cite the section that introduces them rather than a position in the list.
